newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Globus says mulls international share issue.
newsitem.headline: Globus says mulls international share issue.

text.p: The Hungarian canning company Globus Rt is considering an international share offering, the firm's chief executive said.
"We are negotiating (about the share issue), although we are right now at a rather preliminary stage," Miklos Olah told Reuters.
Olah added that the details of the share issue have not yet been decided, but said that Globus expects to raise between one and 3.0 billion forints ($6-18 million).
The money would be used to buy new canneries, he said, adding that Globus is interested in particular in the four plants Hungary's Kereskedelmi and Hitelbank (K & H) intends to sell.

K&H said last month that the four companies - EKO, Arany Facan, SZEKO and Nagyatadi Konzervgyar - have attracted the interest of at least three investors, each of which would like to buy all four. The bank did not name the potential investors.
Olah said that "it's not that we are all that impressed with the quality of these companies' operation, but we need capacity to expand."
In addition, Globus might also buy canneries in Beregovo, Ukraine and Brandenburg, Germany, to help it increase its presence in other east European countries.

Olah said that the new issue may or may not have voting rights. If they are voting shares, then the current biggest owner of Globus -- a consortium of German, Swiss, Austrian and Lichtensteiner investors -- might subscribe a large portion of the issue.
Globus recently began trading in Frankfurt, which Olah said would help the share issue by boosting Globus's prestige.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Globus closed on Tuesday at 2,055 forints.
